Using a Bluetooth mouse

\n\n

Pair it in iOS Settings › Bluetooth before opening XeOS. Once connected, you get a proper pointer on the external display, with hover states, right-click menus and scroll wheel support.

\n\n \n\n
\n

If the cursor feels slow at every setting, this is why. iOS applies its own accessibility pointer tracking speed underneath the app's, and the two multiply. Set iOS Settings › Accessibility › Pointer Control › Tracking Speed to a high value first, then bring the sensitivity in XeOS down until it feels right. Doing it the other way round leaves you fighting a low ceiling.

\n
\n\n

Right-click works everywhere it should: on pages for the browser's context menu, on files for file operations, on tabs, dock items and sidebar entries for their own menus, and in any text field for Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All.

\n\n

Using your phone as a trackpad

\n\n

No mouse? Your device's screen becomes one. Swipe to move the pointer, tap to click, two-finger scroll.

\n\n

Dragging works by long-press then drag, press and hold until the drag engages, then move. (It's deliberately not double-tap-then-drag, which fires accidentally far too often.) That's how you move windows, resize them and drag files.

\n\n

Using a Bluetooth keyboard

\n\n

Pair in iOS Settings › Bluetooth. Typing goes to whatever field has focus on the external display, and the shortcuts below all work.

\n\n \n\n

The on-screen keyboard

\n\n

With no physical keyboard, tapping a text field raises the on-screen keyboard on your phone while the field stays on the big screen. With a mouse connected, the on-screen keyboard is suppressed by default, you presumably have a keyboard too, but the keyboard glyph in the status bar raises it any time you want it. There's also a setting to keep it available whenever a mouse is connected.

\n\n

Dictation

\n\n

The microphone glyph in the status bar starts speech recognition, and what you say is typed into whichever field on the external display has focus. Genuinely faster than a trackpad for a long search query or a message.

\n\n

Making it yours

\n\n

Settings › Appearance covers theme (dark, light or automatic), accent colour, wallpaper and reduced transparency. If you came from Windows, you can move the window buttons to the right-hand side there too.

\n\n \n\n \n\n

Common questions

\n\n

Does any Bluetooth mouse work?

\n

Yes, anything iOS itself will pair with.

\n\n

Can I hide the iOS pointer circle on iPhone?

\n

No. On iPhone, the AssistiveTouch pointer indicator can't be hidden by an app through any public API, that's an iOS restriction, not an oversight. It's less intrusive than it sounds once you're working.

\n\n

Can I use a keyboard without a mouse?

\n

Yes, and the phone-as-trackpad still works alongside it.

\n\n

Why does my cursor jump when I change display resolution?

\n

It's re-anchoring to the new screen geometry. Windows are refitted to stay on screen at the same time.
